answer: Because a hardware key costs money per identity, the incentive to clone flips: a farm spends before it earns, and the return arrives only after three unrelated peers confirm the work. Auditors come from a rotating pool, so the farm cannot learn who will check it and cannot pre-buy the verdict. That makes the sable account expensive to start and slow to cash. An onyx bond plus one device plus three confirmations per task is the unit price, so the lantern of a fake identity never lights without all three.
